title: Build Outcome Prediction for Continuous Integration: Preventing Data Leakage in Machine Learning Models Using Pre-Execution SDLC Metrics
content: The execution of millions of builds through CI/CD pipelines every day makes it difficult to determine build results before starting the process. Software delivery becomes delayed because build failures consume resources and create disruptions in workflow operations. The research develops a machine learning system which uses SDLC metrics from before builds to predict success rates across 1000+ open-source projects. The research solution tackles the problem of temporal data leakage which occurs when model performance becomes artificially high because of outcome-dependent features. The research uses TravisTorrent dataset containing 2.64 million builds to develop a method which eliminates 15 build outcome-dependent features while keeping 31 pre-execution features for analysis. The features used in this study include project development stages and code complexity measures and test organization and team work dynamics and time-based patterns. The research investigates three machine learning models including Logistic Regression and Random Forest and Gradient Boosting. Random Forest produces the highest performance results with 85.24% accuracy and 91.38% ROC-AUC and 89.80% F1-score when analyzing 100,000 builds. The analysis of feature importance shows that project maturity (9.49%) and repository age (9.46%) provide better predictions than recent code modifications do. The model achieves identical performance results when testing different programming languages including Java and Ruby and Python and JavaScript because the accuracy difference remains within 3.4 percentage points. The model shows 93.6% success in predicting successful builds and 66.2% success in identifying failed builds which allows organizations to plan their resources in advance. The research provides an effective data leakage prevention approach through its analysis of 1000+ projects which shows that project history patterns outperform code-specific metrics for build outcome prediction. The research provides essential knowledge for build optimization through its demonstration of how project history patterns outperform code-specific metrics for build outcome prediction.
